gcp._note: is_private=false and linked_network_urns=[] are both BEST-EFFORT DEFAULTS, not directly-observed facts -- google-cloud-dns (the only Google-published Python client for Cloud DNS, and the only one this adapter uses) exposes no visibility/privateVisibilityConfig accessor at all (see gcp_network_mcp.models.dns's module docstring and docs/limitations.md#cloud-dns), so this adapter cannot actually distinguish a public zone from a private one, nor read which networks a private zone is bound to. Defaulting is_private to false (rather than asserting true, which would claim a privacy guarantee this collection never verified) and leaving linked_network_urns empty (rather than guessing prod-shared-vpc) are the least-overclaiming choices available given this structural collection gap. name_servers is populated because, per resources.py::DnsZone's own docstring, GCP always returns its assigned name servers for a managed zone regardless of this visibility gap -- that field IS reliable.
